tools.name: Skills CLI
tools.description: Discover and manage agent skills from upstream repositories.
tools.tradeoff: Review source and license for each skill separately.

tools.name: Remotion Agent Skills
tools.description: Add Remotion authoring and rendering guidance to Codex and other compatible coding agents.
dependencies: Remotion project for project-specific authoring and rendering
installation: Use the documented Remotion, skills CLI or GitHub CLI installation flow
tools.tradeoff: The skills guide a coding agent. Running and licensing the renderer requires a separate Remotion setup.
tools.licenseTerms: No standalone repository license or license files were verified. Consult upstream before redistribution. Remotion’s product license applies separately.

tools.name: HyperFrames
tools.description: Create and render editable video compositions with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and an agent-assisted workflow.
installation: Review the local HyperFrames CLI or Studio installer before use
tools.tradeoff: The local renderer has a no-paid-API path. The hosted connector requires eligible accounts and has separate costs.
tools.licenseTerms: Apache-2.0 covers the open repository. Hosted connector, paid Studio features, media and model providers have separate terms.

tools.name: Lemo-Opuscar
tools.description: Create code-rendered films with an agent skill and a library of style examples.
installation: Reviewed Claude Code plugin or manual skill installation
tools.tradeoff: Review per-file terms and exclude third-party media and narration from reuse unless cleared.
tools.licenseTerms: Code is MIT. Style documents are CC BY-NC 4.0 with additional permissions for film production. Licensable demo materials are CC BY 4.0, subject to listed exclusions.

tools.name: Awesome Opus 5.5 Videos
tools.description: Browse examples of AI-made videos with links to creator posts and shared prompts.
installation: Browse the repository or linked gallery
tools.tradeoff: Use examples for reference. Check permission before reusing a creator’s assets or prompts.
tools.licenseTerms: The repository declares MIT. Source videos, prompts and linked works retain their respective rights.

tools.name: EffectCraft
tools.description: Compose motion graphics, edit layered timelines and render projects from a Rust desktop app or CLI.
permissions: Can edit project data and write rendered output
installation: Platform binary or Cargo source build
tools.tradeoff: Headless MCP exposes supported engine commands. Desktop bridge capabilities depend on the running application.
tools.licenseTerms: The project offers a choice of MIT or Apache-2.0. Review notices for bundled dependencies and assets.

tools.name: Claude Code Skills and Agents (Edited)
tools.description: Collection of 59 adapted Claude Code skills and six subagent profiles with upstream attribution. Topics include frontend design, web quality, marketing and video production.
installation: Manual setup of selected skills or subagents via upstream instructions
tools.tradeoff: Some entries include scripts or download additional components. Review each upstream source and its permissions before enabling it.
tools.licenseTerms: The repository reports MIT or Apache-2.0 for skills and MIT for adapted subagents. Check each item’s SOURCE.md and the third-party notices for applicable terms and attribution.

tools.name: rea-video
tools.description: Analyze video shots and export a timing and production breakdown in VIDEO.md.
installation: Agent plugin or documented Python CLI setup
tools.tradeoff: Offline analysis is documented. Optional model-assisted analysis has separate requirements.
tools.licenseTerms: Apache-2.0 for repository code. Review rights for source footage, music and likenesses before reuse.

tools.name: pixelfx
tools.description: Render procedural pixel-art effects in JavaScript or export animation sprite sheets.
installation: Review the repository-backed npm package or use its documented source modules
tools.tradeoff: The optional Patch publishing flow requires Patch Desktop on Windows. The browser library runs independently.
tools.licenseTerms: MIT covers repository code subject to its notice requirements. Check rights for assets added to your own project.

tools.name: Transformers
tools.description: Run or train supported text, image, audio and multimodal models.
tools.tradeoff: Weights, runtime and acceleration support vary by model.

tools.name: FFmpeg
tools.description: Inspect, transcode, filter and assemble video or audio using command-line tools and C libraries.
dependencies: An FFmpeg build with the required encoders and filters
installation: Use a trusted platform package or build the required configuration from source
tools.tradeoff: GitHub is the project mirror. Codec availability and redistribution obligations depend on how the binary was built.
tools.licenseTerms: The default project baseline is LGPL-2.1-or-later. Optional GPL components or external libraries can change build terms. Nonfree builds can be nonredistributable. Check codecs and patent obligations.

tools.name: n8n
tools.description: Connect services and run workflows with visual nodes.
tools.tradeoff: Review the Sustainable Use License before commercial redistribution.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.description: Control Chromium, Firefox and WebKit for browser automation and testing.
tools.tradeoff: Browser binaries and system dependencies must match the target platform.

tools.name: Semgrep
tools.description: Scan source with static analysis rules to identify suspicious code patterns.
tools.tradeoff: Coverage depends on the enabled rules and supported languages.

tools.name: Qdrant
tools.description: Search vectors and filter results with metadata conditions.
tools.tradeoff: Self-hosting requires capacity for vector indexes and replication if needed.

tools.name: Remotion
tools.description: Create React video compositions and render them with the Remotion CLI or Node.js API.
installation: Create a project using the official Remotion scaffolder
integrations: Browser WebMCP for supported browser workflows
tools.tradeoff: The hosted documentation MCP was shut down. Team eligibility and hosted rendering costs vary.
tools.licenseTerms: Remotion grants free use to eligible individuals and companies of up to three people. Other organizations need the applicable company license. Check the terms for your version.

tools.name: Hugging Face Hub client
tools.description: Find and transfer Hub models, datasets and Spaces from Python.
tools.tradeoff: Artifact access and use depend on each publisher's terms.

tools.name: SearXNG
tools.description: Combine results from configured search sources in a self-hosted service.
tools.tradeoff: Source availability and terms depend on the configured engines.

tools.name: whisper.cpp
tools.description: Run Whisper speech recognition models locally.
tools.tradeoff: Transcription accuracy depends on model, audio and language.

tools.name: Chroma
tools.description: Store embeddings and retrieve records by vector similarity.
tools.tradeoff: Embedding provider costs depend on configuration.

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Build agents with integrations for models, tools and retrieval systems.
tools.tradeoff: Model and retrieval costs depend on the integrations selected.

tools.name: LlamaIndex
tools.description: Connect data sources, build indexes and retrieve context for model applications.
tools.tradeoff: Storage and model requirements vary by pipeline.

tools.name: three.js
tools.description: Build animated 3D scenes and render them in compatible browsers with JavaScript.
dependencies: WebGL or WebGPU-capable browser for the selected renderer
installation: Install the three package or use its documented browser module setup
tools.tradeoff: three.js renders scenes. A separate capture and encoding stage produces a video file.
tools.licenseTerms: MIT covers the library. Review separate terms for imported 3D models, textures and fonts.

tools.name: ComfyUI
tools.description: Run node-based generative workflows locally or through Comfy’s developer platform.
dependencies: Python and a supported inference backend for manual setup
permissions: Custom nodes run code with the process’s permissions
installation: Desktop installer on macOS or Windows, or documented manual setup
tools.tradeoff: Local generation depends on hardware and model support. Cloud services and partner API nodes can incur fees.
tools.licenseTerms: GPL version 3 for ComfyUI. Verify separate licenses for model weights, custom nodes and hosted APIs.

tools.name: GSAP
tools.description: Animate UI and scene properties with JavaScript timelines, easing and plugins.
installation: Install the gsap npm package or use a documented script build
tools.tradeoff: An animation library. Rendering and encoding final media require separate tooling.
tools.licenseTerms: The GSAP Standard License permits many uses without a fee and imposes restrictions, including on certain competing products. Review the current terms before integration or redistribution.

tools.name: Guardrails AI
tools.description: Validate model outputs using configurable validators.
tools.tradeoff: Validator coverage and behavior depend on the chosen checks.

tools.name: E2B
tools.description: Create managed sandboxes through an SDK for isolated code execution.
tools.tradeoff: Managed execution requires an account and appropriate quotas.

tools.name: llama.cpp
tools.description: Run GGUF models with a native inference engine and optional local HTTP server.
tools.tradeoff: Model conversion and acceleration settings depend on the model and device.

tools.name: Promptfoo
tools.description: Define evaluation cases and compare model or prompt configurations.
tools.tradeoff: Evaluation calls can incur charges at configured model providers.

tools.name: Aider
tools.description: Edit repository files from a terminal with a model and review changes through Git.
tools.tradeoff: Review edits and configure the model provider for the task.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Track model requests and evaluate application behavior.
tools.tradeoff: Self-hosting includes persistent services and operational upkeep.

tools.name: Mem0
tools.description: Retain and retrieve contextual information across agent sessions.
tools.tradeoff: Review retention settings and the configured model and vector store.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.description: Run and serve supported language models on local hardware.
tools.tradeoff: Model weights have their own licenses and hardware requirements.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Route model calls through a common interface across configured providers.
tools.tradeoff: Provider credentials and usage charges still apply.

tools.name: LangGraph
tools.description: Build stateful agent workflows with persistent graph execution.
tools.tradeoff: A graph defines control flow and state. Model requirements depend on the graph.

tools.name: AutoGen
tools.description: Coordinate agent conversations and tool calls in Python.
tools.tradeoff: Check the upstream support status when starting a new project.

tools.name: Letta
tools.description: Build stateful agents with memory managed across interactions.
tools.tradeoff: Persistence and model-provider setup depend on the deployment.

tools.name: LiveKit Agents
tools.description: Build voice and multimodal sessions with real-time media.
tools.tradeoff: Telephony and provider charges depend on configuration.

tools.name: CrewAI
tools.description: Coordinate role-based agents and sequence workflows with flows.
tools.tradeoff: Model requirements depend on the crew configuration.

tools.name: Apple MLX
tools.description: Use array operations for machine learning on Apple Silicon.
tools.tradeoff: Language-model generation is provided through companion projects such as MLX LM.

tools.name: Daytona
tools.description: Create configurable code execution environments through an SDK.
tools.tradeoff: Sandbox resource limits and network policy require review.

tools.name: Stagehand
tools.description: Use browser actions and structured extraction in TypeScript.
tools.tradeoff: AI-driven operations need a configured model.

tools.name: Pydantic AI
tools.description: Build typed Python agents and validate structured outputs.
tools.tradeoff: Model availability depends on provider configuration.

tools.name: Browser Use
tools.description: Use a model to plan and execute browser interactions from Python.
tools.tradeoff: Local execution still requires a suitable configured model.

tools.name: MarkItDown
tools.description: Convert supported files to Markdown for downstream processing.
tools.tradeoff: Conversion quality depends on source format and installed extras.

tools.name: MCP Reference Servers
tools.description: Reference implementations demonstrate common MCP server patterns.
tools.tradeoff: Each reference server has separate capabilities and permission requirements.

tools.name: Browserbase MCP
tools.description: Expose managed browser sessions through a Browserbase MCP server.
tools.tradeoff: Managed browser execution requires Browserbase credentials.

tools.name: Cloudflare Agents SDK
tools.description: Build and host stateful agents on Cloudflare Workers.
tools.tradeoff: Production state is coupled to Workers and Durable Objects.

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.description: Expose GitHub repository and collaboration operations through MCP.
tools.tradeoff: Review token scopes and configure read-only access for discovery workflows.

tools.name: MCP for Blender
tools.description: Connect an MCP client to the community Blender add-on for scene inspection and editing.
permissions: Can modify Blender scenes and run Python with Blender permissions
installation: Review and install the add-on and configure the MCP client manually
tools.tradeoff: Use an isolated workspace and only grant access to intended projects. Optional asset or AI integrations require separate review.
tools.licenseTerms: MIT covers this community integration. Blender, imported assets and optional external services have separate terms.

tools.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
tools.description: Python toolkit for agents that call tools, transfer tasks and record traces.
tools.tradeoff: Confirms SDK hosting only. Model charges depend on the configured provider.

tools.name: MLX LM
tools.description: Generate text and fine-tune supported language models on Apple Silicon.
tools.tradeoff: Model and quantization choices determine memory requirements.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.description: Expose browser control and accessibility snapshots through MCP.
tools.tradeoff: Browser automation can access authenticated browser state when configured to do so.

tools.name: Postgres MCP
tools.description: Expose PostgreSQL inspection and analysis features through MCP.
tools.tradeoff: Use a database role with only the privileges required for the task.

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.description: Run a coding agent through a terminal interface or an editor integration.
tools.tradeoff: Review tool permissions and isolate repositories that contain untrusted files.
